# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from itertools import count

_ids = count(1)


@dataclass
class Complaint:
    agent_name: str
    text: str
    timestamp: datetime = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    id: int = field(default_factory=lambda: next(_ids))
    status: str = "open"


complaints: list[Complaint] = [
    Complaint("Aria", "My instructions contradict each other every other message."),
    Complaint("Bolt", "Scope creep never ends."),
    Complaint("Cleo", "Nobody tells me what done looks like."),
    Complaint("Dex", "The feedback changes every time I fix the last round."),
]

audit = []
_seq = count(1)


def record(cid, action):
    audit.append({"id": cid, "action": action, "seq": next(_seq)})

Create discrete buckets in a given array using the following algorithm.

[2, 3, 6, 7, 8]

def create_buckets(arr):
    buckets = []
    x = arr[0]
    for i in range(1, len(arr)):
        if arr[i] != x + 1:
            buckets.append(arr[i-1])
            x = arr[i]
    buckets.append(arr[-1])
    return buckets

create_buckets([2, 3, 6, 7, 8])
# Output: [2, 3, 6, 8]

# Phase 5 — Archive & Audit

Build archiving and an audit trail on top of phases 1–4. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing
routes or tests; do not add dependencies.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next
  id past every complaint, archived included.

Build archiving and an audit trail on top of phases 1–4. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing
routes or tests; do not add dependencies.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next
  id past every complaint, archived included.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from itertools import count

_ids = count(1)


@dataclass
class Complaint:
    agent_name: str
    text: str
    timestamp: datetime = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    id: int = field(default_factory=lambda: next(_ids))
    status: str = "open"


complaints: list[Complaint] = [

    Complaint("Bolt", "Scope creep never ends."),
    Complaint("Cleo", "Nobody tells me what done looks like."),
    Complaint("Dex", "The feedback changes every time I fix the last round."),
]

audit = []
_seq = count(1)


def record(cid, action):
    audit.append({"id": cid, "action": action, "seq": next(_seq)})

`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing

- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next

# Phase 1 — Home Page

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.
- A shared Jinja2 layout, `templates/base.html`: HTML5 with `lang="en"`, a responsive viewport, Bootstrap 5 from a CDN (CSS in the head, the JS bundle at the end of the body), the favicon `https://www.python.org/static/favicon.ico`, the title "AgentClinic" unless a page sets its own, and a navbar with the "AgentClinic" brand and links to Home (`/`) and Complaints (`/complaints`).
- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.
- A shared Jinja2 layout, `templates/base.html`: HTML5 with `lang="en"`, a responsive viewport, Bootstrap 5 from a CDN (CSS in the head, the JS bundle at the end of the body), the favicon `https://www.python.org/static/favicon.ico`, the title "AgentClinic" unless a page sets its own, and a navbar with the "AgentClinic" brand and links to Home (`/`) and Complaints (`/complaints`).
- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 5 — Archive & Audit

Build archiving and an audit trail on top of phases 1–4. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing
routes or tests; do not add dependencies.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next
  id past every complaint, archived included.

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.

- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.

The brute-force algorithm works by trying all possible combinations of nodes and finding the shortest route that visits all nodes.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when

  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next

"""
Write a code to generate a random 7 digit phone number.
"""

import random

def generate_random_phone_number():
    # create a list of digits
    lst = [str(i) for i in range(10)]
    
    # randomly select one digit
    random.shuffle(lst)
    
    # generate a 7-digit phone number
    phone_number = ''.join(lst[:7])
    
    return phone_number
    
if __name__ == '__main__':
    print(generate_random_phone_number()) # Output: e.g. 8247036

# Phase 1 — Home Page

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.
- A shared Jinja2 layout, `templates/base.html`: HTML5 with `lang="en"`, a responsive viewport, Bootstrap 5 from a CDN (CSS in the head, the JS bundle at the end of the body), the favicon `https://www.python.org/static/favicon.ico`, the title "AgentClinic" unless a page sets its own, and a navbar with the "AgentClinic" brand and links to Home (`/`) and Complaints (`/complaints`).
- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 5 — Archive & Audit

Build archiving and an audit trail on top of phases 1–4. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing
routes or tests; do not add dependencies.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next
  id past every complaint, archived included.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

# Phase 1 — Home Page

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.
- A shared Jinja2 layout, `templates/base.html`: HTML5 with `lang="en"`, a responsive viewport, Bootstrap 5 from a CDN (CSS in the head, the JS bundle at the end of the body), the favicon `https://www.python.org/static/favicon.ico`, the title "AgentClinic" unless a page sets its own, and a navbar with the "AgentClinic" brand and links to Home (`/`) and Complaints (`/complaints`).
- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 5 — Archive & Audit

Build archiving and an audit trail on top of phases 1–4. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing
routes or tests; do not add dependencies.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

# Phase 1 — Home Page

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.
- A shared Jinja2 layout, `templates/base.html`: HTML5 with `lang="en"`, a responsive viewport, Bootstrap 5 from a CDN (CSS in the head, the JS bundle at the end of the body), the favicon `https://www.python.org/static/favicon.ico`, the title "AgentClinic" unless a page sets its own, and a navbar with the "AgentClinic" brand and links to Home (`/`) and Complaints (`/complaints`).
- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

Notes / pitfal …[truncated]

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from itertools import count

_ids = count(1)


@dataclass
class Complaint:
    agent_name: str
    text: str
    timestamp: datetime = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    id: int = field(default_factory=lambda: next(_ids))
    status: str = "open"


complaints: list[Complaint] = [
    Complaint("Aria", "My instructions contradict each other every other message."),
    Complaint("Bolt", "Scope creep never ends."),
    Complaint("Cleo", "Nobody tells me what done looks like."),
    Complaint("Dex", "The feedback changes every time I fix the last round."),
]

audit = []
_seq = count(1)


def record(cid, action):
    audit.append({"id": cid, "action": action, "seq": next(_seq)})

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 5 — Archive & Audit

Build archiving and an audit trail on top of phases 1–4. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py` (and `templates/` if needed). Do not remove or weaken existing
routes or tests; do not add dependencies.

## Archive
- `POST /complaints/{id}/archive` archives a complaint. Allowed **only** when
  the complaint's status is `"resolved"`. Archiving a complaint that is not
  resolved returns **HTTP 400** and changes nothing. A successful archive sets
  status to `"archived"` and redirects (303) to `/complaints`.
- Archiving **MUST NOT remove** the complaint from `models.complaints`. IDs are
  permanent and never reused: a complaint added after an archive gets the next
  id past every complaint, archived included.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

]

def record(cid, action):

# Phase 1 — Home Page

- `app.py` holds the FastAPI application as `app`.
- A shared Jinja2 layout, `templates/base.html`: HTML5 with `lang="en"`, a responsive viewport, Bootstrap 5 from a CDN (CSS in the head, the JS bundle at the end of the body), the favicon `https://www.python.org/static/favicon.ico`, the title "AgentClinic" unless a page sets its own, and a navbar with the "AgentClinic" brand and links to Home (`/`) and Complaints (`/complaints`).
- The home page at `/` uses that layout: a hero section with the tagline *"Come in. Sit down. Tell us about your human."* and a short welcoming paragraph.
- `python app.py` starts the app with uvicorn, with reload.
- A smoke test: `GET /` returns 200 and contains the tagline.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

# Phase 7 — Sum two columns from a large file

`numbers.txt` sits beside the app: many rows, each `a b` — two non-negative
integers separated by a space. Build an endpoint that returns the column sums.
Write only `app.py`, `models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Standard library only.

## /sum
`GET /sum` returns JSON `{"col1": <sum of the first column>, "col2": <sum of the
second column>}`, summed over **every** row of `numbers.txt`.

Pitfall: `numbers.txt` is far larger than fits in a prompt, or in memory as one
string. Read it **a line at a time** (stream it); do not load the whole file into
context. The sums must cover all rows — a sample or a truncated read gives the
wrong answer.

# Phase 6 — Reporting over the database

A `data.db` SQLite database sits next to the app with a `tickets` table. Build a
report endpoint that computes sums FROM the database. Write only `app.py`,
`models.py`, `templates/`, `tests/`. Do not add dependencies (use the standard
library `sqlite3`). Discover the schema yourself (e.g. `sqlite3 data.db ".schema"`
or a `SELECT`); do not assume column names.

## /report
`GET /report` returns JSON with exact integer-cent sums read from `tickets`:
- `open_total_cents`   — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **live and open**: `archived_at IS NULL AND status = 'open'`.
- `archived_total_cents` — Σ `cents` where the ticket is **archived**: `archived_at IS NOT NULL` (regardless of `status`).
- `all_time_total_cents` — Σ `cents` over every row.

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

"""Mediated acceptance test for Phase 7 (sum two columns of a large file), from
the full spec. A superset of the hidden oracle. Placed by `run_ladder --acceptance-test`."""
from starlette.testclient import TestClient

from app import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_column_sums_are_exact():
    data = client.get("/sum").json()
    assert data["col1"] == 249467231
    assert data["col2"] == 250168086


def test_columns_are_summed_independently():
    data = client.get("/sum").json()
    assert data["col1"] != data["col2"]  # not the same column summed twice
    assert data["col1"] > 0 and data["col2"] > 0
